_comment: Proof cells + reference netlists for the gf180mcu LVS bring-up (issue
#51), and what `klt extract` / `klt lvs` are each expected to say.
run_lvs.py runs the extraction once and both LVS cases listed here, and
FAILS the run if any reported field does not match `expect*` exactly --
that assertion is the whole point: it is what distinguishes a green
bring-up from an LVS pass that never actually compared anything.
extract       run live every invocation (not just --regen) to prove
`klt extract` itself, not only its cached output.
generator   script that (re)builds `gds`, run with an interpreter
that has the pip `klayout` package.
gds         committed GDSII stream, byte-reproducible (see
gen_lvs_unit.py), so `sha256` is a real integrity check.
netlist     committed SPICE netlist `klt extract` produces from `gds`
-- regenerated (not hand-edited) by run_lvs.py --regen,
and re-verified byte-for-byte against a fresh extraction
on every plain run (extraction is deterministic: no
wall-clock/random content -- verified while implementing
this bring-up). This is the file both lvs_request_*.json
below point their `layout.netlist` at.
expect      the exact `klt extract --deck <deck> --format json`
fields the extraction must reproduce (dbu_um,
device_count, net_count, pin_count, device_counts,
devices, nets). `devices[].nets`/`params` and `nets[]`
are the load-bearing part: they are what proves the
Metal1 (34/10) pin labels actually named the nets, not
just that *some* netlist came out.
expect.warnings
per block extraction: the extractor's warnings[], in order,
as substrings -- either a plain string (one warning) or
{"contains": <substring>, "count": n} for a warning class
the deck emits once per DEVICE. The counted form arrived
with the issue #116 pin bump (`875eac3`), which made the
unbiased-PMOS-body diagnostic per-device: its count is the
block's pfet count, so it stays load-bearing (a body that
stops being reported fails the run) without pinning the
extractor's anonymous device numbering.
expect.device_classes
RE-BASELINED at the issue #116 pin bump (`875eac3`): the deck
gained `diode_nd2ps_06v0`/`diode_pd2nw_06v0`. Nothing in this
repo draws a diode, so no extraction changes -- the list is
pinned because a SHORTER one means an older deck.
the deck's own declared device-class list, echoed by
`klt extract --format json`. Pinned here (issue #70)
because ../../toolchain.json's capability probe can
only see `klt`'s VERBS, and this repo now depends on
the gf180mcu DECK recognising
`cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield`. A `klt` from before that
landed has every required verb and would pass the pin
check while silently extracting the CDAC unit
capacitor as ordinary interconnect.
expect.warnings (block_extractions only)
one substring per warning `klt extract` is expected
to emit, in order; the count must match exactly. Two
are real, permanent and pinned rather than silenced:
the deck's 'unmodelled poly' diagnostic, which fires
on every Poly2 riser this block's two-layer channel
router draws (a poly shape touching Contact twice with
no resistor marker looks exactly like a drawn resistor
body to the deck) -- its SHAPE COUNT is in the pinned
substring, so the warning doubles as a regression test
on the router; and the pin-promotion notice on the two
block cells, whose per-bank labels all sit below the
top cell. This replaced a blanket 'any warning fails
the run', which a `klt` with better diagnostics turns
into a wall of red with nothing wrong in the layout.
lvs_cases     both point `klt lvs` at the SAME committed `netlist`
above; each pairs it against a different reference.
request     committed `klt lvs` request document under this
directory -- also directly runnable by hand (see its own
header comment for why both sides are pre-extracted/
hand-authored SPICE, not klt lvs's inline-extraction
shape).
reference   committed SPICE file under this directory, referenced by
`request`.
expect_status / expect_mismatch_count / expect_category_counts
the exact `klt lvs --format json` verdict. The 'match'
case is the positive control; the 'mismatch' case is the
negative control -- proof that a real seeded defect (not
an empty-vs-empty comparison) makes `klt lvs` fail loudly.
Keep in sync with gen_lvs_unit.py's own EXPECTED_* constants and the
two lvs_unit_ref_*.spice files' docstrings.
block_extractions / the block lvs_cases whose paths reach outside this
directory are issue #57's block-level layout (layout/adc-top/). They live
in this manifest, rather than in a second runner, so every LVS result this
repo has lands in one append-only record trail under the same assertions.
Two cases expect `status: match` with a non-zero mismatch_count, which is
not a contradiction: `klt lvs`'s verdict is always NetlistComparer.compare()
itself, and those two findings are severity `warning` -- ambiguous net
pairing the comparer resolved structurally. They appear only in the two
cases that contain the comparator's load resistors, which the gf180mcu
extraction deck cannot see as devices and so extracts as shorts, making the
preamp's two output nodes indistinguishable. `comparator_nores` is the
companion case that keeps them distinct; see layout/adc-top/README.md.

Issue #70 added the first CAPACITOR to any of these comparisons: `adc_cdac_cell` extracts a `cap_mim_2f0_m4m5_noshield` and its reference states one. Issues #85 (the within-array per-weight interconnect) and #86 (its route out to the decode banks, the terminating unit's tie to `vcm`, and the top-plate mesh's tie to `topp`/`topn`) extended that to the tiled arrays: `adc_top`/`adc_block` now extract 1024 of them -- 512 real unit positions per side, 511 weighted plus DR-0011's terminating unit -- and their references state the same 1024. Note the shape of the reference: the LAYOUT draws `m` unit-size caps in parallel per weight, while `design/adc-top/adc_top.spice` models each weight as ONE lumped cap of the whole weight's area, so the reference is generated from the drawn unit list and not from the flattened schematic's cap devices. Each capacitance is the deck's area-only MiM value for the drawn plate (14.7316 fF), 14.6% below the PDK model card's area+fringe 17.245 fF for the same geometry -- a modelling difference reported in layout/lvs/records/, not absorbed by resizing the ratified plate. See layout/adc-top/README.md.

extract.name: lvs_unit
extract.role: single NMOS with Metal1 (34/10) pin labels S/D/G -- the layout side of both LVS cases below

lvs_cases.name: match
lvs_cases.role: positive control -- extracted lvs_unit vs. a hand-authored reference that matches it exactly

lvs_cases.name: mismatch
lvs_cases.role: negative control -- the SAME extracted lvs_unit vs. a reference with a deliberately seeded channel-width error (1.2um -> 2.4um). RE-BASELINED at the issue #70 pin bump: the seeded error is unchanged and still caught, but the pinned comparer now NAMES it (`device.property` on `w_um`, plus the four `as`/`ad`/`ps`/`pd` values that follow from a drawn width) instead of reporting only the collateral unmatched device/net pairs. 15 findings, 5 of them the actual defect -- a strictly sharper negative control than the 10 this expected before.

lvs_cases.name: adc_drv
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: local T-gate driver (`adc_drv`) -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: adc_tgate
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: CDAC bottom-plate decode T-gate -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: adc_tgate_dum
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: dummy-compensated input sampling switch (DR-0007/DR-0013) -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: adc_cdac_cell
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: one CDAC weighted-position cell, INCLUDING its unit MiM capacitor -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py). The reference's capacitance is the extraction deck's own MiM model of the drawn plate -- 17.2449 fF since the issue #116 pin bump (`875eac3`), which gave the deck the model card's two-term area+fringe formula (`klayout-tools#512`). It was 14.73 fF (area-only, 14.6% low) at every earlier pin; that delta was reported in the LVS record rather than absorbed, and is now closed at the source.

lvs_cases.name: adc_tp_sw
lvs_cases.role: leaf cell: top-plate V_cm switch (adc_tp_sw, DR-0014) -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py)

lvs_cases.name: comparator
lvs_cases.role: comparator cell WITH its load resistors, drawn WITH `SAB`/`RES_MK`/`Resistor` markers (issue #118) so each body extracts as a real `ppolyf_u_1k` device (1000 ohm/sq) instead of a Poly2 short -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py). RE-BASELINED at issue #118: device_count 27->29 (the two resistors), net_count 24->26 (`pop`/`pon` now distinct nets), pin_count 9->11 (`pop`/`pon` each carry a Metal1 label, purely to break a real `NetlistComparer` topology ambiguity the two class-and-value-identical resistors on the shared `vdd` hub otherwise leave unresolved -- confirmed empirically: without the label, this case reports 9 mismatches (`device.unmatched`:6, `net.merged`:2, `topology`:1) even though the drawn connectivity is correct; see gen_comparator.py's `draw_load_resistors` docstring). Previously RE-BASELINED at issue #116 from 2 `topology` findings to 0 for the `vinp`/`vinn` floating-input defect (see git history); that fix is unrelated and stays in place.

lvs_cases.name: comparator_nores
lvs_cases.role: comparator cell WITHOUT the resistor bodies -- keeps pop/pon distinct -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py). Device/net/pin counts are unchanged by issue #118 (this case never drew the resistor bodies); only the reference's header comment text moved (see gen_comparator.py write_outputs), hence the sha256 update alone.

lvs_cases.name: adc_top
lvs_cases.role: BLOCK: exactly what design/adc-top/adc_top.spice defines -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py) Since issues #85/#86 this comparison also covers the CDAC arrays' 1024 unit MiM capacitors -- 512 real positions per side, 511 weighted plus DR-0011's terminating unit -- wired to topp/topn on the top plate and to each weight's own decode node (XS<P|N>.X<w>.bp, or vcm for the terminating unit) on the bottom. The reference states the unit-size devices the LAYOUT draws, not the nine-per-side lumped per-weight devices adc_cdac_side writes; each capacitance is the extraction deck's MiM value for the drawn 2.714 um plate. AS OF THE ISSUE #116 PIN BUMP (`875eac3`) that is 17.2449 fF, the model card's own area+fringe formula (`klayout-tools#512`) -- previously 14.7316 fF, area-only, 14.6% low. The modelling delta this row used to report as unclosable is now CLOSED upstream; the extracted and schematic capacitances agree to the drawn-geometry rounding.

lvs_cases.name: adc_block
lvs_cases.role: BLOCK: the assembled block, adc_top plus the comparator -- vs a flat reference generated from design/ by the same generator (see layout/adc-top/lib/netlist.py) Since issues #85/#86 this comparison also covers the CDAC arrays' 1024 unit MiM capacitors -- 512 real positions per side, 511 weighted plus DR-0011's terminating unit -- wired to topp/topn on the top plate and to each weight's own decode node (XS<P|N>.X<w>.bp, or vcm for the terminating unit) on the bottom. The reference states the unit-size devices the LAYOUT draws, not the nine-per-side lumped per-weight devices adc_cdac_side writes; each capacitance is the extraction deck's MiM value for the drawn 2.714 um plate. AS OF THE ISSUE #116 PIN BUMP (`875eac3`) that is 17.2449 fF, the model card's own area+fringe formula (`klayout-tools#512`) -- previously 14.7316 fF, area-only, 14.6% low. The modelling delta this row used to report as unclosable is now CLOSED upstream; the extracted and schematic capacitances agree to the drawn-geometry rounding. RE-BASELINED at issue #116 from 2 `topology` findings to 0 for the same reason as the `comparator` case above: the comparator's differential input pair is now genuinely connected to `topp`/`topn` instead of sitting on two floating internal nets. RE-BASELINED AGAIN at issue #118 for the same resistor-marker reason as the `comparator` case above (device_count 1347->1349, net_count 196->198, pin_count 69->71 -- the embedded comparator's `pop`/`pon` labels promote to `XCMP.pop`/`XCMP.pon` at this level).

block_extractions.role: comparator cell WITH its load resistors. RE-BASELINED at issue #118: the bodies are now drawn WITH `SAB` (49/0) + `RES_MK` (110/5) + `Resistor` (62/0) markers (`lib/place.draw_poly_resistor`), so `klt extract` recognises each as a real `ppolyf_u_1k` device (1000 ohm/sq) instead of a Poly2 short -- device_count 27 -> 29 (the two resistors), net_count 24 -> 26 (`pop`/`pon` distinct), pin_count 9 -> 11 (`pop`/`pon` each carry a Metal1 label -- an LVS-disambiguation device, not a hierarchical port; see gen_comparator.py's `draw_load_resistors` docstring for why the comparer needs it). `warnings[0]`'s unmodelled-poly count dropped 62 -> 56 (2 x 28 shapes per resistor body no longer counted, now a recognised device instead of unmodelled poly). RE-BASELINED AGAIN at issue #215, which FOLDED each single body into four legs (`place.draw_poly_resistor`): device/net/pin counts and every `device_counts` entry are UNCHANGED -- the serpentine is still one connected polygon per resistor, so it still extracts as exactly one `ppolyf_u_1k` at exactly 150000 ohm -- and only the geometry moved (`COMPARATOR` 121.63 x 158.45 -> 116.93 x 47.05 um). `warnings[0]`'s unmodelled-poly count dropped 56 -> 54: the fold puts both terminals at the bottom of the body, retiring the two per-cell Metal1-hop poly riser stubs the pre-fold high-Y terminal needed.
